title: Every Client Suddenly Rejects the API's Certificate
intro: At 00:00 UTC, mobile apps and partner integrations all started failing with TLS errors against api.example.com. No deploys happened overnight.

steps.prompt: Reproduce it with curl to see the exact error.
steps.fake_output:
* SSL certificate problem: certificate has expired
curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: certificate has expired
steps.hint: curl's verbose output shows the TLS failure reason.

expected_commands: echo | openssl s_client -connect api.example.com:443 -servername api.example.com | openssl x509 -noout -dates
openssl s_client -connect api.example.com:443 -servername api.example.com < /dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates
steps.hint: Pipe the presented certificate into openssl x509 -dates.

steps.prompt: It expired at exactly midnight. Check whether automated renewal was even set up on the server.
steps.fake_output:
Found the following certs:
  Certificate Name: api.example.com
    Expiry Date: 2026-09-28 00:00:00+00:00 (INVALID: EXPIRED)
  (certbot.timer: inactive)
steps.hint: certbot usually renews via a systemd timer or cron job.

steps.prompt: The renewal timer was disabled. Renew the certificate now.
steps.fake_output:
Renewing an existing certificate for api.example.com
Congratulations, all renewals succeeded.
steps.hint: Renew first to restore service; re-enabling automation comes right after.

steps.prompt: Reload nginx so it serves the new certificate, then re-enable the renewal timer.
expected_commands: sudo systemctl reload nginx && sudo systemctl enable --now certbot.timer
systemctl reload nginx && systemctl enable --now certbot.timer
steps.hint: The web server keeps serving the old certificate from memory until it reloads.

resolution: The certificate simply expired: its renewal timer had been disabled (likely during an earlier migration) and nobody noticed for months. Renewing the cert isn't enough on its own — nginx keeps the old certificate loaded in memory until reloaded, which is why 'I renewed it but it's still broken' is a common follow-up. Certificate expiry is the most predictable outage there is, so the real fix is monitoring: alert when any public certificate has fewer than ~14 days left (Prometheus blackbox_exporter's probe_ssl_earliest_cert_expiry, or any uptime service), independent of whether renewal automation says it's working. Automation that fails silently plus no expiry monitoring is exactly how this happens.
